questions.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
questions.description: Return the maximum depth of a binary tree — the number of nodes on the longest path from the root to a leaf. A TreeNode class is provided; the driver builds the tree from level-order input.
questions.inputFormat: One line: the tree in level order, values separated by spaces, "null" for a missing child (an empty line is an empty tree).
constraints: Recursive or BFS solutions are both acceptable.

starterCode.PYTHON:
import sys

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.left = None
        self.right = None


def max_depth(root):
    # Write your solution here
    return 0


def build_tree(tokens):
    if not tokens or tokens[0] == "null":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(tokens[0]))
    queue = deque([root])
    i = 1
    while queue and i < len(tokens):
        node = queue.popleft()
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] != "null":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(tokens[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] != "null":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(tokens[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


def main():
    lines = sys.stdin.read().split("\n")
    print(max_depth(build_tree(lines[0].split())))


main()
